fields.expected: I'm an undergraduate at Johns Hopkins studying Applied Mathematics & Statistics and Economics, and most of my work has been building machine learning systems that have to hold up against real operational constraints. Right now I work on the ML core of an anomaly-detection and alert-prioritization system at Summer Atlantic Capital / SAC Nexus, where I own major parts of the data and ML infrastructure: the event-ingestion pipeline, a versioned FastAPI detection service, temporal sequence modeling over event streams using RNN and Transformer-style approaches, and a learning-to-rank layer for prioritizing alerts. The thing I keep coming back to there is that an anomaly system producing too many alerts creates a second problem instead of solving the first, so I also built a retrieval-augmented explanation layer to make outputs usable by human analysts. Before that, I was lead model developer on a Gates Foundation-funded Hopkins project, training XGBoost models on a national survey dataset of roughly 10 million records, using SHAP for feature selection and interpretation, and designing G-formula causal simulations. I also built an evaluation framework at Intelehealth comparing LLM outputs against a 4,169-case clinical standard using stratified sampling to surface systematic failure modes.
